name: Registered Palestinian Refugee Status (GAPAR)

requirements.blocker_text: Under Law No. 260 of 1956, Palestinian refugees registered with the General Authority for Palestinian Arab Refugees (GAPAR) -- and their descendants -- hold a distinctive permanent legal status in Syria: treated equal to Syrian citizens for public employment, private-sector labor, commercial and property rights (including owning multiple businesses and residential property), military conscription, free government education, and free healthcare at state clinics. A special travel document is issued by the Ministry of Interior (per Law No. 1311 of October 1963) permitting visa-free return to Syria. This is NOT citizenship: registrants retain Palestinian nationality/status and are barred from voting and from holding parliamentary or local-administration office.

evidence_required.document: Proof of descent from a GAPAR-registered refugee

sources.title: Interactive Encyclopedia of the Palestine Question (Institute for Palestine Studies) -- Law No. 260 of 1956's civil-rights framework for GAPAR-registered Palestinian refugees, Law No. 1311 of 1963's travel-document provision, and the explicit exclusions (citizenship, voting, elected office)

GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE MARQUEE ROUTE, MODELED UNDER 'ancestry' RATHER THAN 'humanitarian': this is not an asylum process -- it is a permanent, decades-old, hereditary quasi-citizen legal status assigned by descent from an originally-registered 1948-era refugee population, comparable in structure (though very different in substance) to Ghana's Right of Abode and Pakistan's Pakistan Origin Card built elsewhere in this dataset. Syria's treatment of its Palestinian population is repeatedly described across sources as unusually integrated compared to Palestinian refugees in other Arab host states (contrast Lebanon's far more restrictive treatment, built earlier in this dataset) -- near-full socioeconomic parity with citizens, short of citizenship and political rights. NOT MODELED HERE, since no source in this build addressed it: how (or whether) this status is being administered, reviewed, or altered under the transitional government since December 2024 -- a real open question for a population this large and legally distinctive, flagged for follow-up rather than guessed at.
